title: Positive degree produces a nonzero section with affine nonvanishing locus
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume $\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\chi(C,\mathcal N)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)>0$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Then there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a nonzero global section $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})$ such that its nonvanishing open $C_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] is affine. Tensor powers are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, proof, second paragraph beginning Assume degree positive: growth of sections, finite closed boundary, evaluation kernel, and affine nonvanishing locus (varieties.tex lines 10016-10036).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $C$ is Noetherian and every invertible module on it is coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], its underlying topology is Noetherian (the descending-chain condition for closed subsets). Integrality gives that $C$ is nonempty and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point; this implies the Kolmogorov property, since two points with identical closures would be two generic points of the same irreducible closed subset. Choose a point of $C$ and a nonempty affine open $U$ containing it by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Apply [lem-sc-nonempty-open-complement-finite-dim-le-one] to $U$: the hypotheses are now Noetherian, quasi-sober, Kolmogorov, irreducible and dimension one. Thus $C\setminus U=\{x_1,\ldots,x_t\}$ is finite, and [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed] makes every $x_i$ closed.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, second proof paragraph: choose a finite closed boundary with affine complement; expanded using Tags 01IS and 01IT and the existing dimension-one topological lemmas.

proof.text: For each $x_i$, properness includes finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Choose a finite-type affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ containing $x_i$ using the affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The closed point corresponds to a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i$ (its closure in the spectrum is $V(\mathfrak m_i)$). Its residue field is $A_i/\mathfrak m_i$ [def-weil-residue-field], which is generated over $k$ by the images of any finite algebra-generating family of $A_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] to conclude $d_i=\dim_k\kappa(x_i)<\infty$. Put $B=\sum_{i=1}^t d_i\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$, with $B=0$ if $t=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, second proof paragraph, parenthetical Nullstellensatz argument; Algebra Tag 00FV, theorem-nullstellensatz (1).

proof.text: Put $d=\deg_k(\mathcal N)>0$ and $a=\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$. Tensor products of invertible modules are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], so induction gives invertibility of $\mathcal N^{\otimes m}$ for every $m\ge0$. Its degree is $md$: the base case is $\deg_k\mathcal O_C=a-a=0$ by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]; in the induction step [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] gives $\deg_k(\mathcal N^{\otimes(m+1)})=\deg_k(\mathcal N^{\otimes m})+d$. Rearranging the definition of degree yields $\chi(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes m})=md+a$. No ampleness or smoothness is used.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, displayed growth formula; Tag 0AYX, lemma-degree-tensor-product, rank-one case.

proof.text: For each $m$, the module $\mathcal N^{\otimes m}$ is coherent by [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent]. Its cohomology is finite-dimensional and its Euler characteristic is the alternating sum of the cohomology dimensions by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined]. Since $C$ is Noetherian of dimension one, [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^q(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes m})=0$ for $q>1$. By the definition of sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], $H^0=\Gamma$. Hence $h^0_m=\dim_k\Gamma(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes m})=md+a+h^1_m\ge md+a$. Since $d$ is a positive integer, take the integer $n=B+|a|+1\ge1$; then $nd+a\ge n+a\ge B+1>B$, and therefore $h^0_n>B$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, displayed growth formula and the strict dimension inequality; Cohomology Tag 02UZ, proposition-vanishing-Noetherian, and Cohomology of Schemes Tags 02O5 and 02O6.

proof.text: Let $V=\Gamma(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})$ and form the $k$-linear evaluation map $e:V\to\prod_{i=1}^t\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(x_i)$, $s\mapsto(s(x_i))_i$, taking germs and then reducing modulo the maximal ideal. Local rank-one trivializations [def-sc-invertible-module] identify each fibre with $\kappa(x_i)$ as a vector space over that field, so the target has $k$-dimension $B$: concatenate a $k$-basis of each of these finitely many factors. Because $\dim_k V>B$, evaluation cannot be injective: the images of a basis of $V$ would otherwise be a linearly independent family larger than a basis of its target. Thus there are distinct vectors with the same evaluation; subtracting gives $0\ne s\in\ker e$. In particular $s(x_i)=0$ for every $i$. This is elementary finite-dimensional linear algebra, not a surjectivity assertion about $e$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, second proof paragraph: hence we can find a nonzero section vanishing at all boundary points.

proof.text: By the definition of the nonvanishing locus [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], the equalities $s(x_i)=0$ imply $C_s\subseteq C\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_t\}=U$. Apply [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] to the affine open $U$ and the section $s$ of the invertible module $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$. It says $U\cap C_s$ is affine; this open equals $C_s$ by the containment just proved. The integer $n\ge1$ and the nonzero section $s$ therefore have exactly the required properties.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, end of second proof paragraph, explicitly applying Properties Tag 01PV, lemma-affine-cap-s-open.
